newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Coffee leads commodities markets lower.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Coffee leads commodities markets lower.

text.p: Commodities prices mostly slid lower on Thursday, coffee leading the fall in a market characterised by thin trade all round.
Attempts by copper and aluminium to claw higher were beaten back on the London Metal Exchange (LME), while another upside failure by zinc sent base metals prices sliding.
Aluminium suffered from fund selling to close at $1,609 per tonne, down $26.5, while zinc stumbled $45 lower to finish at $1,259 per tonne.
Copper proved unable to break through solid resistance and turned around from its high of $2,380 to give up all its gains and close at $2,340, down $29.
Coffee's slide came as the market went hungry for fresh fundamental inputs to feed on.
Benchmark London May robusta futures closed down $31 at $1,610 per tonne, eroding gains made on Wednesday.

But traders said that while the coffee market would continue to swing wildly, the near-term prospects remained bullish on the back of tight nearby availability. On Wednesday, the market seemed to have priced in news of a port strike in Santos, Brazil.
Cocoa followed coffee lower in light volume as investors took profits. A jittery opening in New York opened did not help either.
Sugar managed to stage a lone rise among soft commodities in London, inching higher in more active trade.
The precious metals had a tough time, with silver at first suffering from a bout of fund selling before later bottoming out.
Gold slid in the wake of the silver sell-off and closed at $348.65 per ounce, down $2.70. Platinum and palladium also closed lower.
Analysts said gold was looking less attractive as a fall in crude oil futures as the winter heating season ended and lower stock market values signalled a weakening in inflationary pressures.
IPE May Brent futures suffered, falling some 30 cents to around $18.20 per barrel.
On the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) wheat futures eased while soybeans also opened lower.
